claims.text: Conventional refractory HEAs typically include W, Ta, and Mo.
W, Ta, and Mo are high-activation refractory elements.
W, Ta, and Mo form long-lived radioisotopes under neutron irradiation.
Ti, V, Cr, and Fe are low-activation refractory alternatives to W, Ta, and Mo.
Replacing W, Ta, and Mo with Ti, V, Cr, and Fe can produce a refractory HEA.
Compositional adjustment will maintain phase stability in the modified alloy.
Compositional adjustment will maintain grain refinement in the modified alloy.
Phase stability and grain refinement contribute to mechanical integrity.
Phase stability and grain refinement contribute to irradiation resistance.
The replacement elements form only short-lived isotopes under neutron irradiation.
Replacing elements that produce long-lived radioisotopes with elements that produce short-lived isotopes reduces residual activation.
Careful compositional balancing can preserve the high-temperature mechanical properties typical of refractory HEAs.
Careful compositional balancing can preserve the irradiation tolerance typical of refractory HEAs.
The proposed low-activation HEA will have high-temperature mechanical performance comparable to conventional refractory HEAs.
The proposed low-activation HEA will have irradiation resistance comparable to conventional refractory HEAs.
The proposed low-activation HEA will accumulate fewer long-lived radioactive isotopes under neutron irradiation than conventional refractory HEAs.
Conventional refractory HEAs containing W, Ta, and Mo are mechanically robust at high temperature.
Conventional refractory HEAs containing W, Ta, and Mo are irradiation resistant.
Conventional refractory HEAs containing W, Ta, and Mo have high residual activation levels.
Changes in temperature, dose rate, or phase stability may alter the proposed alloy's performance.
